clue.text: Has his order changed for condiment?

indicators.note: the letters of 'has his order' are changed round into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone's table order has been switched, and they wonder which sauce or relish they got instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order changed' reads as a muddled meal order; 'changed' is the anagram signal working on all three of the first words.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent root grated into a sauce served with roast beef, so it is a classic condiment.

clue.text: Frontier without British arrangement

indicators.note: without means the letter for British is left out of the frontier word

parts.note: a frontier is a border between countries

explanation.surface: A border agreement made with Britain left out of the negotiations.
explanation.definitionFit: Order is a synonym of arrangement, as in putting books in alphabetical order.

clue.text: Loading goods finally using tug

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word goods

parts.note: using a tug, or pulling something along, is towing

explanation.surface: A dockside scene: cargo is at last being loaded with the help of a tugboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tug' looks like the boat; here using a tug simply means pulling, towing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stowing cargo means packing it away aboard, which is loading it.

clue.text: Perhaps Titian nude for sketch again

parts.note: Titian is a reddish-auburn shade named after the painter, so an example of red
in the raw means naked, so raw stands for nude

explanation.surface: An art student is told to make another sketch of a Titian nude.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian suggests the Venetian painter of nudes; here it is the hair colour, an example ('Perhaps') of red.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw a picture is to draw or sketch it a second time.

clue.text: Cobblers possibly tense standing up

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the word for tense is read from bottom to top

parts.note: tense means stressed, anxious

explanation.surface: Shoe-menders, perhaps, getting nervous while working on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: A cobbler is also a baked fruit pudding with a scone topping, hence 'possibly': one example of a sweet course.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit cobbler is one kind of pudding, so cobblers are examples of sweet courses.

clue.text: Sopranos broadcast missing a 'godfather'

indicators.note: broadcast suggests scattering, so the letters of Sopranos are scattered and rearranged
missing tells us the letter a is absent from the rearranged word Sopranos

explanation.surface: A broadcast of the mob drama The Sopranos lacks its godfather figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sopranos is a TV mafia series, which makes 'godfather' look like a mob boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent formally vouches for a child at baptism, and a sponsor is one who stands surety in that role.

clue.text: Score with men helping around box

indicators.note: around means the soldiers and the portion are placed either side of the box word

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers who are not officers
a helping is a portion, a ration
a chest is a large box

explanation.surface: Men helping to shift a box round to settle a score, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like a tally or grudge; it is the musical sense. 'around' means the men and the helping sit either side of the box.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is the written arrangement of music for an ensemble, which is what an orchestration provides.

clue.text: Most faithful perplexed about lock

indicators.note: about means the word for perplexed surrounds the lock

parts.note: to be lost is to be bewildered, perplexed
a Yale is a well-known brand of door lock

explanation.surface: The most devoted person is baffled by a stubborn lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyal means faithful, and this is its superlative form.

clue.text: It's vital to keep team winning

indicators.note: to keep means the urgent word holds the team inside it

parts.note: something that is vital is pressing, urgent
a posse is a group of people, a team, as in Western films

explanation.surface: A coach insists it's vital to keep the team together for a winning season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winning' looks like a sporting result; it is the adjective meaning charming.
explanation.definitionFit: A winning manner is an attractive, appealing one, the sense of creating a favourable first impression.

clue.text: Sat on back of bronco here?

definitions.text: Sat on back of bronco here?

parts.note: to have ridden a horse is to have sat on it

indicators.note: back of points to the last letter of the word bronco

explanation.surface: A question asking whether this is where someone sat astride a bucking horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the event: riding a bronco is what happens here.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowboys ride bucking broncos at this kind of competitive show, so the place fits the riding described.

clue.text: Dirty look threatening after nightclub

indicators.note: after means the threatening look comes after the nightclub in the answer

parts.note: a disco is a nightclub
to lour is to frown or look menacing, as a dark sky does

explanation.surface: Someone gives a menacing filthy look as they leave a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty look' reads as one phrase; split it so 'Dirty' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To discolour something is to stain or soil it, which is to dirty it.

clue.text: Hideaway in Channel Island, period without technology

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the island and period sit outside the technology letters

parts.note: Herm is one of the smaller Channel Islands, between Guernsey and Sark
an age is a period of time
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A retreat on a Channel Island where one can live for a while without modern gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but has its old sense of outside, so the island and period enclose the technology.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit's dwelling is a secluded retreat, a place to hide away from the world.

clue.text: Small instrument for cutting

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: A little tool designed for cutting things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrument for cutting' suggests a blade; the instrument is musical, and 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp blade is a cutting one, keen-edged and able to slice.

clue.text: Something tasteless or dull getting eaten initially

definitions.text: Something tasteless or dull getting eaten initially

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A description of bland, heavy food being eaten first.
explanation.walkthrough: The initial letters of the six words before 'initially' spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, filling food with little flavour, or by extension dull, turgid material.

clue.text: Found Iron Age building employing spades

indicators.note: employing means the rearranged letters take in the spades letter
building suggests putting together, so the letters of Iron Age are reassembled

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games such as bridge

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finds an Iron Age building by digging with spades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find; it is the verb meaning to establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To found a society is to establish or set it up, which is to organise it.

clue.text: More cutting on board making tapas?

indicators.note: on, as in being on a ship, means the sharper word is carried inside the ship letters

parts.note: board points to SS, steamship, the vessel one boards in crosswords
tarter means sharper or more acidic, as a more cutting remark is

explanation.surface: Sharper knives on the chopping board are needed for preparing Spanish snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: In cryptic convention 'on board' puts a piece inside SS, a steamship; 'board' here is not a chopping board.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are small dishes, so they can serve as the first course or appetiser of a meal; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Risk tip on needle

parts.note: a tip is an end or point
to needle someone is to anger them

explanation.surface: A warning that the point of a needle is dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needle' looks like a sewing pin but is the verb meaning to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: To risk something is to put it in danger, to imperil it.

clue.text: Queen maybe describes this compiler's band

indicators.note: describes in its sense of drawing round, so the ruler's word encircles the setter's letters

parts.note: a regent rules in place of a monarch; a queen could be one, hence maybe
the setter refers to themself, so this compiler's is I'M, I am

explanation.surface: The setter boasts that Queen, the rock group, is their favourite band.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen looks like the rock band; it is an example of a ruler, a regent. 'describes' means draws a line around.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment is a large body of soldiers, and band can mean an organised group of people.

clue.text: Waspish matron fussing round head of department

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the department letter
fussing suggests agitation, so the letters of matron are stirred about
head of points to the first letter of the word department

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued hospital matron fusses about the head of department.
explanation.definitionFit: Mordant wit is biting and sarcastic, so it is close in sense to stinging or spiteful.

clue.text: Fly in jet set section

indicators.note: in means the answer lies within the run of letters jet set section

explanation.surface: A wealthy socialite flies first class with the jet set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' and 'jet' suggest air travel, but the answer is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The African insect that spreads sleeping sickness is a bloodsucking type of fly.

clue.text: Varnish the woman will put on account

indicators.note: put on means, in a down answer, the woman's word sits above the account letters

parts.note: she will is contracted to she'll

explanation.surface: A woman decides to buy varnish on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin from the lac insect used to make a hard glossy finish for wood.

clue.text: Starved, destined to eat last of scraps

indicators.note: to eat means the destined word swallows the scraps letter

parts.note: fated means destined

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the word scraps

explanation.surface: Someone half-starved is fated to live on leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Having fasted, one has gone without food, so has deliberately starved.

clue.text: Singer's note for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means the word is as heard by listeners

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote

explanation.surface: A singer hits a note for the listeners in the hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks musical; it is British money. A tenner is a ten-pound note. 'Singer's' is read as 'singer is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with a high voice, so the term names a singer.

clue.text: Sense a battle with European head

parts.note: war is armed conflict, a battle on a bigger scale
a ness is a headland or promontory, as in Loch Ness's Inverness

explanation.surface: A sense of a European fighting a battle with a commander at its head.
explanation.walkthrough: Ness, a headland, appears in British place names such as Shoeburyness.
explanation.definitionFit: Awareness is perception or consciousness, the faculty of sensing something.

clue.text: Almost doesn't start in good time

indicators.note: doesn't start means the word for almost loses its opening letter

parts.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: A latecomer almost fails to begin on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive in good time is to be ahead of the deadline, not late.

clue.text: Millions laugh, talking about Blitz

indicators.note: about here means the answer lies spread about inside the words millions laugh, talking

explanation.surface: Millions of people laugh, chatting about the wartime Blitz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talking about' reads as one phrase; 'about' alone signals the concealed answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A blitz is a sudden, intense attack, and an onslaught is a fierce assault.

clue.text: Old actress learning name

parts.note: lore is knowledge or learning handed down

explanation.surface: A veteran actress learning a name for a part.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophia Loren is a classic Italian film star, an actress of the older generation.

clue.text: Unusually a pretty cold old reptile

indicators.note: unusually means arranged in an unusual way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A strangely attractive, cold-blooded ancient creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges A PRETTY, the C for cold and OLD together.
explanation.definitionFit: This flying creature of the dinosaur age was an extinct winged reptile.
